subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what blocking/background/config rules should constrain it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects reset latency, silent tool execution, durable memory persistence, and plugin/config contracts, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Approve bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Define a reset-memory policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat session-memory hook improvements such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 as the supported reset boundary and narrow this issue away from silent agent execution.

options.title: Defer to memory plugins
options.body: Require memory plugins or MCP-backed memory services to own continuous persistence and only extend core events where current plugin APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Define a reset-memory policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail connects this decision to the original reset behavior and the pre-compaction flush primitive.
